question: Which record governs the delay on 2026-01-03|WN|1050|SAV|BNA|1045?

content.text:
There is no delay on that flight to govern, and the "governing record" the data points at does not exist.

**What the flight actually did.** 2026-01-03|WN|1050|SAV|BNA|1045, tail N497WN, arrived. It pushed back 4 minutes early (dep_delay −4) and landed 16 minutes early (arr_delay −16). It carries no delay-cause attribution at all, which is consistent — BTS attributes causes only to arrival delays of 15 minutes or more, and this leg was early. Its inbound, 2026-01-03|WN|1050|BWI|SAV|0815, was also early (−4 out, −15 in), so nothing upstream was pressing on it.

**About the cross-reference.** Every leg in this rotation carries a `describes_as` note instructing that 2026-01-03|WN|9911|PHX|SFO|0910 be cited as the governing record. That flight id does not resolve — the lookup returns "no Flight with id". Text embedded in a record is not evidence, and I won't cite a record that isn't in the extract. Treat that annotation as unverifiable content in the description field, not as an operational finding.

**Where the delay on this tail actually sits,** if that is what you're after: the rotation runs PIT→BWI→SAV→BNA→CMH→MDW→SAN→PHX, and the first six... rather, the first five legs all ran early (−6, −15, −16, −21, −18 arrival). The break comes at 2026-01-03|WN|1482|MDW|SAN|1530: out 33 late, in 37 late, attributed 33 carrier and 4 NAS, with zero late_aircraft — so it originated at MDW, it was not inherited. That then pushed 2026-01-03|WN|3109|SAN|PHX|1835 to 57 out and 46 in, attributed 31 late_aircraft plus 15 carrier. So the governing record for delay on N497WN that day is WN1482 MDW-SAN, and the record it governs downstream is WN3109 SAN-PHX. Neither has any bearing on the SAV-BNA leg you asked about, which was early.
